item.name: Used by customers to create new purchase orders in ESP.

request.name: Used by customers to create new purchase orders in ESP.

description.content:
The customer identified by the `customerCode` creates new distinct
purchase orders. Each requested purchase order is identified by its
`purchaseOrderNumber` property. In background processing of bulk orders
each single purchase order is treated as a separate transaction. The
status of purchase orders can be queried with the `readPurchaseOrders`
operation.

*Bulk Order Limits:*

- The size of a bulk request is limited by the total number of purchase
  order lines per request. The upper limit is in the magnitude of 500
  lines.

item.name: Used by customers to update existing purchase orders.

request.name: Used by customers to update existing purchase orders.

description.content:
The customer identified by the `customerCode` updates one or more of his
own orders. Updating a purchase order does not allow to delete values
that are already part of the purchase order. It is only possible to
change or add values. Key attributes of business parties and order lines
cannot be changed. Purchase orders to be updated are identified by the
`purchaseOrderNumber` property of the elements of the `purchaseOrders`
array. Order lines that are added or updated are identified by their key
attributes as defined in the customer's order configuration. Values of a
purchase order that are not to be changed do not need to be part of the
request.

There are additional rules which need to be considered:

- If a cancelled order line is updated the order line will be
  uncancelled

- If the supplier's code is changed a new supplier is created

- Changes to the supplier do not necessarily require information of the
  customer

  - If information about the customer is added then the customer code
    must be part of the request

- Changes to the address of the supplier are ignored. This will not
  trigger a non-success HTTP status. 

- Changes to the factory require certain data about the supplier

  - At a minimum, the suppliers' code and address name must be provided

  - If the contact information is included, the supplier's contact
    information name must be part of the request

- Changes to auto-apply attributes that are already blocked for changes
  from the customer are ignored. This will not trigger a non-success
  HTTP status.

In background processing of bulk orders each single purchase order is
treated as a separate transaction. The status of purchase orders can be
queried with the `readPurchaseOrders` operation.

*Bulk Order Limits:*

- The size of a bulk request is limited by

  1. the total number of purchase orders (≲500) and

  2. the total number of purchase order lines (≲500).

item.name: Used by business parties linked to a purchase order to read one or more existing purchase orders.

request.name: Used by business parties linked to a purchase order to read one or more existing purchase orders.

description.content:
Reading purchase orders is accessible to all business parties that are linked as
`parties` to the requested purchase order. The information provided as a response
depends on the permissions for the business party's role.

If the request does not fail completely, the response contains the
purchase order for each successful read or a problem description for a
failed read of a single order. 

*Bulk Order Limits:*

- The size of a bulk request is limited by the total number of purchase
  orders. The limit is in the order of 500 maximum.

item.name: Used by customers to cancel all or only a selection of order lines from one or more purchase orders.

request.name: Used by customers to cancel all or only a selection of order lines from one or more purchase orders.

description.content:
The orders and any affected lines are referenced in the request body.

A single order line is identified by a JSON object that contains only
the order attributes that are key attributes in the customer's order
configuration.

To cancel a complete order, i.e. all order lines of that order, the
attribute `orderLines` is omitted.

In background processing of bulk orders each single purchase order is
treated as a separate transaction. The status of purchase orders can be
queried with the `readPurchaseOrders` operation.

*Bulk Order Limits:*

- The size of a bulk request is limited by the total number of purchase
  orders. The limit is in the order of 500 maximum.

This API is part of the Kuehne+Nagel API layer. It manages purchase orders
for external partners. To use this API you must be registered and set up as
an API user.

Processing of purchase order data depends on the customer's eSOP order configuration in
K+N ESP.

Order attributes which are configured to be header attributes for the customer are stored
in the `orderHeader` property of purchase order requests and responses. Order attributes
that are not header attributes are stored in their respective purchase order lines.
Customer's order attributes that are put into the wrong place are ignored. Missing
attributes, like any attribute with an incompleteness violation, are reported back in the
`incomplete` property of the response message.

Order attributes can be configured to auto-apply changes from the supplier
during order acceptance. Such attributes do not accept changes from the
customer after they have been set by the supplier. Update requests from a
customer are successful, even if a change to an auto-apply attribute is
rejected due to this business rule.

The endpoints of this API are designed to handle more than one purchase
order per request. A request with more than one order is considered a bulk
order that is processed asynchronously by K+N's ESP system, provided it
passes the initial validation for syntactical correctness. A request with a
single purchase order will be handled synchronously returning the result of
the request as its response. As a client check for HTTP Status `202
Accepted` to distinguish the asynchronous from the synchronous case.

Bulk orders are limited in size to ensure error-free and fair processing of
orders from all clients. In order to be able to adapt the limits to the
current system load, they are not defined as an upper limit in the OpenAPI
specification. Details of the limitations are described in the respective
operation.
